note: Derived from domain/capability-topology.json. Hand edits are refused: validate_arrival_engineering.py re-derives these bytes and compares.

arrival-ledger.claim: per-capability record of the highest arrival an actual receipt supports; a claim above the recorded level is a finding, and levels rise only by receipt readback

cadence-run-denominator.claim: the cadence sweep's first live run named checks=15, which is the five bundles admitted before it; a sixth bundle admitted after that run has never been in one

closure-by-pointer.claim: findings terminate in a durable home some process re-reads; the closure law itself is pointed at in its owner, never restated here

consumer-less-core.claim: offline-provable cores and __main__ probe scripts with zero consumers on any of the five surfaces, found by hand in one dispatcher session

dangling-pointer.claim: cross-repo interface pointers naming probe interfaces whose carrier has been adjudicated retired upstream, with nothing in the pointing repository re-reading them

false-documented-pin.claim: a module header claiming its tool pins are mirrored in a lock file whose live bytes carry no such entries

five-surface-audit.claim: an audit that reads one surface answers declaration, not arrival: the driver enumerates imports, value_flow, ci, adapter and cli_text and reports the surface set

planned-island.claim: a verb a consumer may remember to call, and a retrieval slice with no consumer surface at all, are islands being planned rather than found

retired-carrier.claim: the upstream retirement adjudication that makes every row pointing at that carrier a maintain-on-event trigger

shared-exit-cure.claim: the canonical cure: bind the capability to an exit the consumer already traverses and make the consumer's receipt inadmissible without it
